near_miss.lead: ON faðir ok móðir ~ Ved. pitā ca mātā ca / Lat. matribus et patribus (father-and-mother binomial)
near_miss.why_not: Cognate kin binomial but universal; ON contexts are Christian church-law (baptism, paternity, godparenthood), partners are charms/epic morality; no shared collocation beyond the pair itself.

near_miss.lead: triad móðir/systir/dóttir as forbidden women ~ MBh mātṛvat svasṛvat duhitṛvat (other men's wives treated as mother, sister, daughter)
near_miss.why_not: Context is genuinely congruent (sexual restraint), but the ON lists are canon-law incest degrees (Leviticus-derived) and the triad of closest female kin is natural anywhere; no figure beyond the kin terms.

near_miss.lead: konungs dóttir / systir ~ duhitā vasūnām; ORu брат брата... мати дъчери polyptoton
near_miss.why_not: Genealogical statements; the ORu polyptoton is the biblical end-time topos (Mark 13:12) with no ON counterpart in the pivot.

near_miss.lead: ON ǫl (ale brewing measured by sáð) ~ Latv. miežus sēju ... alutiņš; salds alutiņš
near_miss.why_not: *h2elut- is a known Germanic-Baltic lexical isogloss, but no shared wording: ON is a law on ale-brewing quotas / saga Yule feast, Latvian a sowing and drinking song; sweet-ale epithet absent in ON.

near_miss.lead: ON fyrirfara friði sínum ok fé (forfeit peace and property) ~ Ved. priyaḥ ... paśūnām
near_miss.why_not: fé ok friðr is an inner-Germanic legal binomial (outlawry); Vedic priya- + gen. paśūnām is adjective + genitive 'dear to cattle', a different relation and context.

near_miss.lead: rautt gull 'red gold' (helmet) ~ lohita ... hiraṇya kavaca; rautt sem blóð
near_miss.why_not: collocates_8c --pair red~gold: 36 Germanic hits, Indo-Iranian only this MBh line (red face, golden armour: not 'red gold'), Russian krasno zoloto not cognate. Red-gold is Germanic; 'red as blood' universal.

near_miss.lead: kalla/œpa svá hátt at ... megi heyra (call loud enough to be heard)
near_miss.why_not: Procedural legal formula; Hittite ḫalzai and Catullus auris share no cognate wording.

near_miss.lead: bundinn lausan / binda ~ Lat. soluo, pecus; Skt baddhvā ... paśuṃ
near_miss.why_not: Shared roots only (bind, loose, *peḱu-); thief led bound vs Cato's sale lex vs simile of a tethered beast: no common collocation.

near_miss.lead: hefna bróður síns; skǫmm at flýja; ráða bana; hjálm bítr; lágu um nætr
near_miss.why_not: Partners share only common roots; ON phrases (revenge, shame of flight, cause death) have no cognate wording in the partners.

search_lead.cognate: ON nafn ~ Gk ὄνομα (*h1nómn̥); predicate renewed: ON mun aldrigi týnaz 'will never be lost' vs Gk ἄφθιτον / ἀθάνατον
search_lead.argument: Þiðreks saga says of the dead Sigurðr that his name will never perish (in German speech or among Norsemen), as reward of strength and courtesy; Theognis promises Cyrnus an imperishable name. Same topos (hero's/addressee's name outliving death) with cognate noun; cf. Hávamál orðstírr deyr aldregi (recalled). Weak: Þiðreks saga is a late translation-literature text, and the verb is not cognate; the stronger IE formula is with *ḱléwos, not the name.

error.correct_reading: móður, acc./dat. of móðir 'mother' (barn skal móður fylgja)
error.evidence: Same clause in AM-78-4to 29v:1 (w224/554) reads 'barn skall moðor fylgía'; móðr 'wrath' makes no sense here.
